checks.claim: P:tube-wiener-realization, measurability and regression: countable Hahn-Banach norming family, Borel coordinates, Bochner conditional expectation without RNP, X_j equal to the sum of W(e_l)Ce_l, and X_j to X in L2(B).
checks.reason: Hand-checked. Coordinates give l(E[X|G_j]) = sum W(e_l)<k_l,e_l> = l(sum W(e_l)Ce_l), and the norming family lifts this to B. The conditional norm inequality and scalar Jensen give the L2 contraction on simple variables. Monotone-class event approximation gives convergence. Finite-dimensional and zero H stabilize or are trivial.

checks.claim: P:tube-wiener-realization, Cameron identification: ker C = H_seen perp, injectivity on H_seen, first chaos W(H_seen), norm ||P_seen h||, X in E0 almost surely, Hahn-Banach restriction to E0.
checks.reason: l(Ch) = <k_l,h> gives the kernel and injectivity. This matches the first-chaos definition printed on p.190 (h = E[XZ], norm E[Z^2]^(1/2)). The finite sums lie in C(H), so an almost surely convergent subsequence puts X in closed E0. k_l depends only on l restricted to E0.

checks.claim: P:tube-wiener-realization, tightness and full support: finite closed ball unions with summable error give a compact set and a Radon law; the tail is independent of the head; the positive-ball argument holds for singular head covariance.
checks.reason: The errors sum to epsilon over j>=0. The intersection is closed and totally bounded, hence compact. Tail labels (I-P_j)k_l are orthogonal to e_1..e_j, so joint Gaussianity and countable Borel coordinates give independence. C is bounded, so CP_jh tends to Ch. The preimage under the finite linear map is open about the coefficient vector of P_jh, and the standard Gaussian charges it. The triangle inequality with the epsilon/3 splits and closure give support equal to E0.

checks.claim: P:tube-wiener-realization, measurable norm: V_j, finite orthonormal h_k perpendicular to V_j are perpendicular to e_l, regression and Jensen tail bound, epsilon cubed then Markov, isometry onto H_CM, excluded subspace C(V_j), completion E0, characteristic functional.
checks.reason: <h_k,e_l> = <h_k,P_seen e_l> = 0. Conditional coordinates are sum W(h_k)<(I-P_j)k_l,h_k> = sum W(h_k)l(Ch_k). Jensen then gives second moment below epsilon^3, and Chebyshev gives probability below epsilon, uniformly over families. C is isometric from H_seen, so C h_k are CM-orthonormal. Density in E0 and the characteristic functional exp(-||k_l||^2/2) identify the law. This is genuine abstract Wiener eligibility, not a formal covariance bound.

checks.claim: PRIMARY import: Theorem 11.6 is quoted faithfully as a set-enlargement theorem, and Theorem 11.7/Example 11.8 are not used.
checks.reason: Compared with both exact images and the excerpt. Hypotheses (E,H,mu), Borel A, mu(A)>0, a-hat in (-infinity,infinity], conclusion mu((A+rK)^c) <= barPhi(a-hat+r), and the tail estimate for y>=0 all match printed p.190. The theorem is labeled as imported. The only imprecision is the footnote pinpoint, recorded as a minor finding.

checks.claim: L:tube-closed-geometry: compact closed ball images, closed tubes, {d<=r} = T_r including r=0, lower semicontinuity and Borel measurability.
checks.reason: Coordinate diagonal extraction and Fatou give a weak limit in the ball, compactness plus scalar testing gives norm convergence of images, and closed plus compact is closed. With ||h_j|| <= r+1/j the weak limit has norm <= r and closedness of A gives attainment. Sublevel closedness gives lsc.

checks.claim: L:tube-closed-geometry: exact CM ball K = C(Ball1) = sqrt(delta)Mean(Ball1), T_r = A + (r/sqrt(delta))K, and P(d(X)>r) <= exp(-r^2/(2 delta)).
checks.reason: P_seen maps the raw unit ball onto the H_seen unit ball and C kills the complement, so the identity is exact, not an embedding upper bound. Markov gives mu(A)>=1/2, so a-hat>=0 or +infinity. Then barPhi(a-hat + r/sqrt(delta)) <= exp(-(a-hat + r/sqrt(delta))^2/2) <= exp(-r^2/(2 delta)). The enlargements are closed, so no outer-measure reading is needed.

checks.claim: P:tube-rayleigh-transfer: domination for every Borel nondecreasing G including jumps, open/closed/zero endpoints, infinite expectations, no measurable control selection, zero law with F(0) not assumed zero.
checks.reason: Upper level sets are upper intervals. {d>=c} is the decreasing intersection of {d>s}, which gives the closed-endpoint bound for c>0. Rayleigh has no atoms, and c=0 gives probability one on both sides. Layer cake works in [0,infinity] without subtraction. Attainment gives F(X) <= G(d(X)) on the full-measure set {d finite}. E exp(G(R)/delta) is exactly the displayed integral. The zero law follows from F(0) <= G(0) <= G(r) and normalization.

checks.claim: Parameter compatibility: same SA theta, r_t and p ranges, all three fixed-Q guards before delta, for all original models including alpha=d=1 and white noise.
checks.reason: theta<1-a/2 gives 1/(1-theta)<2/a; theta>1/2 gives r_t>2 and nu in (1,2); alpha+a<2 makes the theta and gamma ranges nonempty; 1-1/r_t>theta. Q is fixed in E:radius-anchor-Q before delta. No model restriction is added.

checks.claim: P:tube-actual-law, Banach and Gaussian hypotheses: separable little C^theta K(E) product with exact delta-p norm, zero-start, stopped at the true length, empty block zero, jointly Gaussian on the same W, finite L2 norm.
checks.reason: Finite-rank rational matrices and polygonal paths give separability of the closure only, as stated. Finite coefficient paths are zero-start, Lipschitz and compact-valued, and stopping is a bounded map preserving this. Statistics are L2 limits of joint first-chaos variables. Pullback isometry makes W_m isonormal, so path moments apply (see minor pointer finding). No block independence is used.

checks.claim: P:tube-actual-law, supported labels: every statistic has k_l in H_I without assuming global basis tests are supported.
checks.reason: Stopped rows have slow support in [0,1], and L:cameron-actual-residual approximates endpoints inside I. Its projected-transfer argument at J=0 gives F-tuple labels in H_I. Composition with bounded E compression (A i = i M_E) covers E statistics. The alternative coordinate route is also valid: a first-chaos variable measurable for completed sigma(W(H_I)) has its label in H_I.

checks.claim: P:tube-actual-law, mean and covariance: compressed mean compact at each fixed R, uniform norm M_0||C_t||, primitive bounded into the tuple, compact Mean_delta, E[X W(Phi)] = sqrt(delta) Mean_delta Phi with mask and covariance once.
checks.reason: E:uniform-mean-row is the E restriction of E:cameron-spatial-row, so T_R U equals the compression of T by dense tensors. r_t lies in (2,2/a), as the parents require. Compact conjugation, affine pullback and 1-1/r_t>theta give a bounded primitive. E:cameron-actual-covariance at J=0, compressed as in P:symplectic-block-mean, gives the identity with scale g_delta delta^(a/2) = sqrt(delta). No uniform-R compactness is claimed.

checks.claim: P:tube-actual-law: b_delta <= C delta^((1-a)/2-d/Q) tends to 0 at R_delta = 1/delta + 2, from the SA anchor with zero projection.
checks.reason: P:radius-mean-anchor with Pi=0 is exactly this tuple and norm, p>=1. R_delta<=3/delta because delta<1, and Q>2d/(1-a) gives a positive exponent. The other two guards are used in the path moment bound.

checks.claim: L:tube-actual-endpoint, global functional: F_delta is finite and continuous on all tuples, with the true product order, partial and empty last factor.
checks.reason: Linear Young is everywhere defined and locally Lipschitz on B(E), with norm-one multiplication and arbitrary driver. The delta-p norm is equivalent to the product norm at fixed delta. Fixed free factors, finite products, the norm and log max are continuous. ell_N=0 gives the identity factor.

checks.claim: L:tube-actual-endpoint, restart: the actual global E endpoint equals the ordered product, using one retaining slow source, same pullbacks, mask, amplitude and massless phase before limits, then E/F intertwining.
checks.reason: Hand-checked E:raw-block-restart. T_{delta,0}[f(.-mB)] = T_{delta,m}f; conjugated driver increments equal X_m; Young uniqueness gives P_glob(mB+u,mB) = D_m^0(u). Stopped and unstopped drivers agree on [0,ell_m]. Composition with L = NB + tau gives the product. Ai = iM, S_F i = iS_E and U_F i = iU_E restrict it to E, and injectivity of i finishes. The eta^2 mask is admissible and even. No GL rate, GLF finiteness, independence, mask commutation or point trace enters.

checks.claim: L:tube-actual-endpoint, baseline: SP at W_fast, T=L_delta, c=g_delta, Phi=0 gives norm at least one, so exp(F(X)/delta) equals the actual squared operator norm.
checks.reason: This is exactly the instance written in P:symplectic-raw. P*JP=J with ||J||=1 forces ||P||>=1 almost surely, which removes the maximum. The identity is pointwise in delta and supplies no uniform budget.

checks.claim: P:tube-coarse-envelope, primitive and Young steps: delta sum h^r_t <= (C_pr C_mean)^r_t ||Phi||^r_t, C_pr <= 18B^(3-1/r_t), and log||U_d|| <= c_Y(1+d^nu) for any tuple error.
checks.reason: Recomputed: ||f||_{L^r(0,ell)} <= G_B^2 delta^(-1/r) t_m. The sup bound B^(1-1/r) and seminorm bound B^(1-1/r-theta) give the constant, and delta h^r <= C_pr^r t_m^r. The true partition sums to the field norm, and no sqrt(delta) remains. G_B<=3B gives 18B^(3-1/r_t). E:young-upper-refined-growth with d<=1+d^nu, or E:constant-young-growth with (1+d)^nu<=2^(nu-1)(1+d^nu), gives c_Y(B,theta), independent of R and delta.

checks.claim: P:tube-coarse-envelope, constants: the F bound, weighted power means, D0, D1, D2 and C_env, for all admissible delta and R>=1.
checks.reason: Recomputed: 2 times 2^(nu-1) c_Y gives 2^nu c_Y. Mathlib form (sum f)^q <= n^(q-1) sum f^q at q=p/nu>=1 and q=r_t/nu>1 with f = norm^nu >= 0, raised to 1/q and multiplied by delta, gives exactly (delta n)^(1-nu/p)||a||^nu and the r_t analogue. p=nu gives exponent zero on a positive base. N>=1 gives n>=2 and delta n<=2/B, with nonnegative exponents. log G_B>=0 makes the upper expression nonnegative. C_env depends on neither delta nor R.

checks.claim: P:tube-coarse-envelope, conclusion: G_delta finite, nonempty sup, monotone, Borel, no attainment; tube theorem gives the actual second operator moment bound; zero law direct.
checks.reason: a=0 and Phi=0 are admissible, F>=0, and the bound gives finiteness. Monotone implies Borel. The definition is exactly F<=G(r) on T_r, and F is continuous on E0. Combining P:tube-rayleigh-transfer with E:tube-global-endpoint gives the moment bound. It is not a sharp constant or point moment. The zero case has G constant equal to F(0).

minor: Citation pinpoint: Footnote 3 is printed entirely on p.190 in the exact image. Page 191 only continues Theorem 11.7. The TeX and target phrase 'footnote on pp. 190-191' is imprecise; it has no mathematical effect because all enlargements are proved closed.

Pointer precision in P:tube-actual-law: finite L2 norm for the pulled-back noise W_m is best cited through C:radius-covariance-residuals (or the isometry that makes W_m isonormal) rather than P:radius-actual-moments alone. Separability of H_I (L:cameron-supported-tensor) is used without a pointer.

Wording in P:tube-actual-law: only Q>2d/(1-a) gives positivity of the exponent. The other two guards serve the path moment bound behind the anchor, so 'three guards make the exponent positive' could be sharpened.

L:tube-actual-endpoint does not say that (35.10) holds almost surely, and it does not state the zero-covariance case, although its RB parent section fixes a nonzero covariance. The missing case is immediate from the free group law and the free norm baseline noted after P:symplectic-block-mean; the next proposition's direct zero case uses it.

P:tube-rayleigh-transfer leaves the null event {d=infinity} implicit in the layer-cake step, where the source says explicitly that it may be assigned any value. This is harmless because d is finite almost surely.

P:tube-coarse-envelope attributes 1<=G_B to P:uniform-actual-cameron, which states only the upper bound; the lower bound is the trivial v=0 case. 'Earlier growth bounds' has no label and could name E:young-upper-refined-growth and E:constant-young-growth. E_{0,delta} and 'admissible delta' are used without a local definition, though their meanings are unambiguous from E:tube-covariance-scale and the Section 29 partition.
